claims.text: Ethics is the set of moral principles that guides how a person acts; for a computing professional it governs decisions about data, systems and people that the law alone does not reach.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A professional body such as the BCS or the IEEE publishes a code of conduct that its members agree to follow, and membership signals to employers and clients that the professional works to a stated standard.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Acting unethically can damage people directly - leaked personal data, a careless safety system - and it damages the professional and the profession's reputation, so the impact runs past the act itself.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Acting ethically builds trust: users supply honest data and rely on systems built with care, so the professional's work carries weight and the profession keeps its standing.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Copyright legislation gives the creator of a work the legal right to control how it is copied, adapted and distributed, so software, like a book or a song, belongs to its maker unless the right is assigned away.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Copyright is needed because software can be copied exactly at almost no cost, so without the right to control copying a creator's work could be taken and sold by anyone and creating would stop paying.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A software licence sets what a user may do with the software: free software (Free Software Foundation) gives the freedom to run, study, change and share the source; open-source software (Open Source Initiative) makes the source available under terms allowing use, change and redistribution; shareware is free to try with payment expected if it is kept; commercial software is sold for a fee with the source closed.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A licence is justified by the situation: free or open-source suits work that must be inspected, changed and shared and a user with the skills to maintain it; commercial suits software whose source is the vendor's business and where a contract must answer for faults; shareware suits a small tool a user can try before paying.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Artificial Intelligence is the making of systems that perform tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as recognising speech and images, learning from data and making decisions.

claims.text: AI's impact has social, economic and environmental sides: socially, its judgements affect people directly; economically, it shifts work while creating new work; environmentally, building and running large systems consumes power and resources.
